text:
Aisha: Heads-up — saw a cluster of tail latency spikes this morning tied to prefetch + handoff between GPU pools and host-backed staging. Spike pattern looks like: normal tokens, then a ~60–120ms pause, then a burst.
Tom: Repro steps? where on the stack do you think it's happening — kernel, our offload layer, or the runtime scheduler?
Aisha: Repro with internal loadgen shows pauses when a tenant goes from gpu-resident to host-backed then back within the same request sequence. Seems correlated with 'handoff' code path where we serialize KV cache and issue host staging.
Liam: Do you have logs or traces? try enabling the handoff counters I added in the last PR (hand_off_ms, prefetch_wait_ms). That PR wasn't rolled out cluster-wide though.
Aisha: Pasted a snippet of a typical trace:

```
[2026-03-21T09:12:34.123Z] serve: req=0x7f, stage=ENCODING
[2026-03-21T09:12:34.187Z] offload: start handoff tenant=acme seq=2048
[2026-03-21T09:12:34.250Z] offload: kvcache flush done
[2026-03-21T09:12:34.370Z] prefetch: wait_for_host_pool(tenant) -> 120ms
[2026-03-21T09:12:34.372Z] serve: resumed, tokens=.. burst
```

Aisha: That prefetch wait looks like the source.
Sara: Is the host pool admission gating synchronous? If we block the inference thread on host pool allocation that's obviously bad. We should be able to handoff async and continue other tenants.
Tom: Current handoff flow: runtime calls pool->acquire(blocking) in the same thread, copies, then returns. We assumed acquire would be cheap but host-backed allocations can stall (NUMA, page faults, remote DMA). We need to decouple.
Priya: Long-term refactor idea: make handoff produce a Lease object and enqueue a deferred copy task on a background offload worker. The inference pipeline holds a placeholder until the KV region is ready but can continue filling other worker slots. That reduces tail latency at the cost of more complex bookkeeping.
Liam: We must be careful: placeholders + async copy means we need deterministic KV cache semantics so cache hits mid-request behave right. Also can't blow up memory with many pending leases.
Aisha: Agreed. For short-term mitigation: increase hysteresis threshold so we avoid bouncing between pools rapidly. Add a cold-time penalty: once demoted to host for < N ms, pin for M ms.
Tom: I tried increasing demote_grace_ms from 50 -> 250 in staging and saw drop in spikes but overall host pool pressure rose. So it's a tradeoff.
Priya: We can also try a non-blocking acquire with a fast-fail path that instructs runtime to fallback to a cheaper model variant (lower memory) when host allocation would block. That leverages our routing/fallback policy.
Sara: Yeah — fallback + async handoff combo is probably the most robust: immediate fallback for latency-sensitive requests, async handoff for non-critical ones.
Liam: Instrumentation: we need three new telemetry keys emitted per request: handoff_attempted, handoff_block_ms, fallback_triggered. Also histograms for host_alloc_latency.
Aisha: I'll add those metrics to the perf PR. For reproducer: use loadgen with seq=2048, batch=4, inter-arrival=20ms, and enable forced demote frequency=0.3. Command: `python tools/loadgen.py --seq 2048 --batch 4 --qps 50 --force-demote=0.3`
Tom: Can someone check if kernel page-faults spike on the host nodes during handoff? I want to rule out upstream VM behavior (lazy commit/page-in).
Priya: I checked node metrics — page faults do rise but only partially explains 120ms waits. There's also occasional slow NVMe-backed staging write latencies.
Aisha: Next steps I propose:
- short term: add metrics + increase demote hysteresis on canary
- mid term: implement non-blocking acquire + immediate fallback policy
- long term: refactor handoff into Lease + background offload workers and formalize lease lifecycle API
Tom: OK. I'll own the non-blocking acquire + fallback POC. Priya, can you own the canary config and metrics dashboard?
Priya: Yes. I'll also throw alerts for any handoff_block_ms > 50ms.
Liam: I'll start a design doc sketch for the Lease lifecycle (ownership, cancellation, memory accounting, GC) and post an RFC follow-up.
Sara: When you write the RFC include corner cases: cross-tenant fairness, pending-lease memory caps, crash/restart semantics.
Aisha: Thanks all. If POC shows clear win we can roll to prod next week. infra-bot: deploy-canary started for tag=hand_off_mitigations-2026-03-21
infra-bot: deploy status: succeeded on 3/5 canaries, failed on node node-17 (OOM during increased hysteresis test) — rollback enacted :warning:
Aisha: Noted — Priya, can you exclude node-17 from the canary and re-run? It might be special-cased (smaller host RAM).
Priya: Will do. Re-running now.
Tom: I'll open a ticket to track the Lease refactor and link to this thread. Treat this as follow-up to allocator handoff area.
